front.title: Cryptographic Context Compaction Receipts, Sensitivity Label Inheritance, and Verifiable Right-to-Be-Forgotten Lineage for Agent Memory

abstract.t: Long-running autonomous AI agents periodically summarize, compact, and distill episodic interaction logs into persistent vector or graph memory stores. Lossy context compaction erases the cryptographic provenance of which source documents contributed to a compacted memory state, stripping enterprise sensitivity labels (DLP classifications) and making regulatory data-erasure mandates (GDPR Article 17 Right to Erasure / CCPA purge) impossible to verify. This document specifies the Ephemeral Context Compaction Receipt (ECCR) protocol: a Merkle inclusion and label-ceiling receipt that preserves deterministic sensitivity inheritance and cryptographic purge verifiability across lossy memory compaction boundaries.

section.name: Introduction and Problem Statement
section.t: When an agent summarizes 50 conversational turns and 12 retrieved enterprise files into a single compacted memory embedding or summary node, existing provenance formats (W3C PROV, SCITT) lose the cryptographic link between the pre-compaction source digests and the post-compaction memory artifact. Consequently, a HIGHLY_CONFIDENTIAL document can be silently laundered into an unlabeled memory summary, or survive a mandatory regulatory deletion tombstone.

This specification complements the foundational execution-trace verification architecture defined in draft-durga-agenttrust-trace-verification-00 by introducing deterministic, fail-closed wire semantics specifically addressing Ephemeral Compaction & Privacy Lineage.

section.name: Normative Fail-Closed Verification Rules
section.t: Conforming verifiers and relying-party gateways MUST enforce the following deterministic invariants before releasing any downstream side effect:

ol.li: LEAST_UPPER_BOUND_LABEL_INHERITANCE: The inherited_sensitivity_ceiling of a compacted memory artifact MUST equal the strict least-upper-bound (maximum sensitivity dominance level) of all pre-compaction source items included in source_items_merkle_root.

CRYPTOGRAPHIC_TOMBSTONE_PROPAGATION: If any source item included in source_items_merkle_root receives a regulatory purge tombstone, the memory store MUST invalidate compacted_output_hash and re-compact over the remaining non-tombstoned leaves, emitting a new superseding ECCR.
RETENTION_CEILING_BINDING: The retention_purge_epoch of the compacted artifact MUST NOT exceed the minimum expiration timestamp among all contributing source items.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: All pre-image objects MUST be canonicalized using RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) prior to signature generation or verification under RFC 8032 Ed25519. Any clock skew exceeding 60 seconds, digest mismatch, or missing cryptographic binding MUST cause the verifier to fail closed and emit an auditable security rejection receipt.
